utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Please be seated. Good morning to everybody. Good morning, ladies and gentlemen; good morning to the technical booth, to the interpreters; good morning to the legal assistants and court reporters, the Prosecution and the Defence. I see that Mr. Jovan Simic has something to communicate. Mr. Jovan Simic, please go ahead.

utterances.speaker: MR. J. SIMIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, Your Honour. I apologise for raising this matter, which I think is probably a matter for the Status Conference, but in view of the urgency, I should like to present it now. The fact is the following: My client, Dragoljub Prcac, is in a poor state of health. There are problems which he has had from the beginning of the trial. He has very strong headaches, and it has already been ascertained that he has a very high blood pressure. We have tabled a request to the Registrar to enable him to have a medical specialist examination, and we should like to request that in view of his health situation and his age, and to avoid any untoward effects which could slow up these legal proceedings, to enable him to be taken out of the court earlier than the end of the day. The Trial Chamber has tabled a decision that Mr. Prcac should be taken with the other accused, transported with them. This means that he has a problem. He has to wait for two to two and a half hours after the trial proceedings and he is not able to take his medicines and have his therapy and a rest on time, and then he is brought to the Tribunal two to two and a half hours earlier. So I should like to prevail upon this Trial Chamber to either revoke that ruling -- and as we are hearing witnesses, then I don't see that this could be an impediment -- or in some other way to influence the Registrar, because we have tabled a written request along those lines, to enable Mr. Prcac to have his health treated, and this would enable him to attend the court proceedings. Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Simic, the ruling was not a ruling of this Trial Chamber but it was a ruling by the Registrar, and I am going to ask the registrar to take note of what Mr. Simic has just said so that steps can be taken to rectify matters. Would you take note of that, Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much, Mr. Jovan Simic, for bringing that to our attention, this problem, and I'm sure that the Registrar will do everything in her power to remedy the matter. As I say, this is not a ruling of this Trial Chamber, but the Trial Chamber will be making its recommendation along those lines to the Registrar. Having said that, I think that we can have the witness brought in. Is that not so, Madam Hollis? Just one moment, please, Mr. Usher. I think Mr. O'Sullivan would like to say a few words. Let us hear Mr. O'Sullivan first.

utterances.speaker: MR. O'SULLIVAN
utterances.text: Your Honour, I note that Judge Riad is not on the bench. We're into day five of his absence. My understanding is that his absence was due to the Celebici appeal which has finished. I believe the hearings are through in Celebici and Judge Riad is still not back. We're now into day five, as I said, of his absence, and under Rule 15 bis (A), paragraph (A) contemplates a three-day absence and we're now into day five.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. You are right in so much as the fact that Judge Fouad Riad is not present here in the courtroom, that is quite right. We were working within the frameworks of Rule 71 and not 15 bis, and this Rule does provide for various illnesses, that is to say, urgent personal business or illness. If these are not the reasons, then we propose that the parties function under Rule 71. The other applied to Rule 15 bis. You are quite right that the Celebici proceedings are not ongoing today, but as you know, they have not been completed yet, and I think they will be continuing into next week. So Judge Fouad Riad, as we all note, is not here; that is quite right. I did not think of that myself. Either we can continue under the same terms that we have functioned in the past, that is to say, governed by Rule 71, or we cannot go ahead. Those are the two options, and I now put them to you. Do you agree that we continue under the same terms that we did in the previous days, the past week? Can we continue? If not, then we'll have to adjourn. What is your position? Let us hear Ms. Hollis.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOLLIS
utterances.text: Your Honour, the Prosecution has no objection to continue to operate in the fashion we have been operating the other four days of this week.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] What about the Defence? Mr. Krstan Simic has the floor.

utterances.speaker: MR. K. SIMIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, we gave our agreement before the beginning of this trial, but I have not had a chance to consult the Defence team of Mr. Kos. The last row agrees that we continue with the proceedings without the presence of Judge Fouad Riad, as we have been doing for the past few days, but I would like to hear the opinions of the Kos Defence team.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. Are there any objections? As you know, the Judges' work does not only include work in the courtroom. They have other obligations to attend to as well. But let us hear the Defence. Do they have any objections to make? I see no -- Mr. O'Sullivan.

utterances.speaker: MR. O'SULLIVAN
utterances.text: We do not object to proceeding under Rule 71. However, for the record, we state that it is of fundamental importance to have a full Bench, so that all the Judges are present during the trial. And circumstances arise, but we urge the Trial Chamber to make that the exception. And that is our position, that it becomes problematic as we go more and more -- further and further without a full Bench.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In any case, Mr. O'Sullivan, I would like to say that if this is a fundamental objection not to continue -- I think this is an exception. Now, would you like to continue nonetheless, or not?

utterances.speaker: MR. O'SULLIVAN
utterances.text: We will continue. We will accede to that request and repeat that we urge that the full Bench return.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOLLIS
utterances.text: Excuse me, Your Honour, but could we have a clarification for the record? Is Defence counsel saying that they are acceding or that they are, in fact, consenting to this? There is a connotation that is different, and we want the record clear so that it does not become an appellate issue. So if we could have an unequivocal response, we would certainly appreciate that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So with that nuance, do you accept -- do you accept and accede -- do you accept? You agree and you accept?

utterances.speaker: MR. O'SULLIVAN
utterances.text: That's correct, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you for your understanding. As I said from the beginning of the week, the Trial Chamber proposed this manner of proceeding to expedite matters, and having said that, we are going to continue, as all parties are in agreement and accept this. Let me say that I would like to thank you, Mr. O'Sullivan, for drawing our attention to that matter. I think that we are now able to have the witness shown in. Would the usher please do so.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, witness. Can you hear me properly?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. I hear you very well, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Do you feel better today?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I feel excellent, thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. You're going to continue answering the questions put to you by Mr. Krstan Simic. Mr. Krstan Simic, your witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. K. SIMIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. K. SIMIC
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. Mrkalj. We're going to continue and try and be a bit more efficient. During your testimony you frequently made mention of the rules regulating conduct for members of the police force in performing their duties.

utterances.speaker: EDIN MRKALJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did speak about that.

utterances.speaker: MR. K. SIMIC
utterances.text: Could you tell the Court, please, the full name of that legal act, those rules and regulations?

utterances.speaker: EDIN MRKALJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: The rules are the rules of conduct and the performance of duty for the public security service.

utterances.speaker: MR. K. SIMIC
utterances.text: Thank you. When you worked in the public security station of Prijedor, did you have an appointment paper, that is to say, appointing you to your job, work post?

utterances.speaker: EDIN MRKALJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: When I got my job, I received a decision on employment.

utterances.speaker: MR. K. SIMIC
utterances.text: Over time, did you receive any new decisions, new assignments or duties? In order to speed matters up and to help you, I should like the usher to show a document to the witness. It is Exhibit D8/1, and the English version is D8A/1. Mr. Mrkalj, you have a decision before you which was brought in at the beginning of 1990, when the transformation of the OSUP took place. Did you get a decision like this yourself?

utterances.speaker: EDIN MRKALJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: May I read through this decision?

utterances.speaker: MR. K. SIMIC
utterances.text: Yes, please do. Go ahead.

utterances.speaker: EDIN MRKALJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have read it.

utterances.speaker: MR. K. SIMIC
utterances.text: Did you receive a decision of this kind as to your employment and duties?

utterances.speaker: EDIN MRKALJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. K. SIMIC
utterances.text: Could you tell the Court what your actual work post was, that is, the professional formulation that we have here?

utterances.speaker: EDIN MRKALJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I remember, in those decisions, the decision said that I was a policeman, a security technician, assigned to the Prijedor Police Station.

utterances.speaker: MR. K. SIMIC
utterances.text: Can you tell us: In the police service, what organ or which individual was in charge of distributing the employees in the police?

utterances.speaker: EDIN MRKALJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: How do you mean?

utterances.speaker: MR. K. SIMIC
utterances.text: Well, the structure of the police, from the police chief downwards.

utterances.speaker: EDIN MRKALJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: You mean as far as the work posts were concerned or the assignments?

utterances.speaker: MR. K. SIMIC
utterances.text: Well, yes. Who gave the members of the police force their assignments?

utterances.speaker: EDIN MRKALJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: I received my assignment in the secretariat by a decision of the ministry. Now, what actual duties I would have, my concrete duties, my commander, the commander of the police station, that was his job to assign me actual tasks and duties.

utterances.speaker: MR. K. SIMIC
utterances.text: So the ministry determines your work post; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: EDIN MRKALJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. You didn't understand me. The ministry sends me to the police station of Prijedor. That is my decision. I was assigned to the police station in Prijedor.

utterances.speaker: MR. K. SIMIC
utterances.text: Yes. So that is your status; your work post was there?

utterances.speaker: EDIN MRKALJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was assigned to assignments and duties within the Prijedor local police station.

utterances.speaker: MR. K. SIMIC
utterances.text: Well, the ministry didn't tell you that you would be a technician for security?

utterances.speaker: EDIN MRKALJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: But I already was. That was the training that I received at school.

utterances.speaker: MR. K. SIMIC
utterances.text: You worked in matters of security.

utterances.speaker: EDIN MRKALJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. K. SIMIC
utterances.text: And then you got a decision. You were given a written decision saying that you would be working as a policeman in security matters.

utterances.speaker: EDIN MRKALJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, that was work that is part of my job.

utterances.speaker: MR. K. SIMIC
utterances.text: Well, thank you. Yes. You also spoke about disciplinary measures, and you passed over that very speedily.

utterances.speaker: MR. K. SIMIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We can have this document returned now.

utterances.speaker: MR. K. SIMIC
utterances.text: In the legal system from which the two of us have come, did different disciplinary -- was disciplinary action taken in different ways? Did different disciplinary procedure exist?

utterances.speaker: EDIN MRKALJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. K. SIMIC
utterances.text: For example, disciplinary action within a firm, a company, a public security station? Did they differ?

utterances.speaker: EDIN MRKALJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, disciplinary action was taken.

utterances.speaker: MR. K. SIMIC
utterances.text: What about disciplinary action with disciplinary courts before magistrates? Were cases filed there, and the basic criminal courts, depending on the seriousness of the crime in question?

utterances.speaker: EDIN MRKALJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. K. SIMIC
utterances.text: You said that policemen too, just like every other individual, were subject to disciplinary responsibility and disciplinary proceedings if they committed an offence violating one of the laws and regulations, depending on the competencies of the different organs we mentioned; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: EDIN MRKALJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. K. SIMIC
utterances.text: Let us now speak about disciplinary action within the police organisation, the public security station. Were you ever a member of any disciplinary committee during your work in the police force?

utterances.speaker: EDIN MRKALJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I was not.

utterances.speaker: MR. K. SIMIC
utterances.text: During your work in the police force, was any disciplinary action taken against you?

utterances.speaker: EDIN MRKALJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. K. SIMIC
utterances.text: In disciplinary action and procedure in the police force, who is authorised to punish a policeman for an offence of any kind and violating his duties as a member of the police force?

utterances.speaker: EDIN MRKALJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I remember, there was a set procedure.

utterances.speaker: MR. K. SIMIC
utterances.text: Who decides on punishment? Who brings in the decision to punish a policeman when this procedure, this prosecuting procedure, and disciplinary procedure is put into force?

utterances.speaker: EDIN MRKALJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Could you explain what you mean by "punish," "punishment"? What do you mean?

utterances.speaker: MR. K. SIMIC
utterances.text: Well, let me put it this way: There's a disciplinary action brought against a policeman because, for example, he was drunk when on duty. It was ascertained that he was drunk and he is punished for that because he has violated the rules which you so keenly stipulated. So who is the individual who says that that member of the police force is guilty, and for being guilty he is punished in such a way with a disciplinary measure? Who takes that decision in the police force?

utterances.speaker: EDIN MRKALJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, in case of an offence of that kind, when the facts are ascertained, it is the superior, the superior officer who decides on punishment.

utterances.speaker: MR. K. SIMIC
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Asked by Ms. Hollis about a concrete, specific question, where somebody was killed as a result of an action, according to the standards that prevailed in the police force and the legal system, did that imply -- a man is dead; does that imply criminal proceedings or a disciplinary action?

utterances.speaker: EDIN MRKALJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, criminal proceedings.

utterances.speaker: MR. K. SIMIC
utterances.text: So for violations of that kind, criminal proceedings are initiated; that is what you said. Thank you very much. Let us go back for a moment to your own experiences in those days. You said that you stopped working in the police, or rather the public security station, to be quite precise in our terminology, on the 10th of April, 1992.

utterances.speaker: EDIN MRKALJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. K. SIMIC
utterances.text: As far as I remember, the chief of the public security station at the time was Hasan Talundzic. Did you in any way inform any of your superiors that you no longer wanted to work in the police? Did you submit a request for termination of employment?

utterances.speaker: EDIN MRKALJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: I personally remember what I said. I said that on the 10th I stopped working, which means that I appeared at the station and said that I was on sick-leave, and after that I no longer appeared at work.

utterances.speaker: MR. K. SIMIC
utterances.text: Did you officially open sick-leave with the competent medical institution?

utterances.speaker: EDIN MRKALJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. K. SIMIC
utterances.text: According to the rules and customs in force at the end of the month of April, did you bring to your office medical reports to justify your absence and for your salary to be calculated accordingly?

utterances.speaker: EDIN MRKALJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't bring any certificate. From the moment I went on sick-leave, I was on sick-leave, so should there be any changes in the sense of me recovering, I would automatically have to come to work. But from that date on, I was registered as being on sick-leave.

utterances.speaker: MR. K. SIMIC
utterances.text: If I understood you correctly, and I think I did, it follows from what you said that in the system in force at the time, it was sufficient to say, "I'm on sick-leave" and you're on sick-leave, without having to bring any kind of certificate or report that goes into your files certifying this sickness.

utterances.speaker: EDIN MRKALJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did bring a certificate and handed it in regarding the beginning of my sick-leave.

utterances.speaker: MR. K. SIMIC
utterances.text: Very well. Thank you. From the 10th of April on, you kept your personal weapons, an automatic rifle and a pistol; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: EDIN MRKALJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. K. SIMIC
utterances.text: Do you know a policeman called Aziz Aliskovic?

utterances.speaker: EDIN MRKALJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I knew him.

utterances.speaker: MR. K. SIMIC
utterances.text: Was he a member of the public security station of Prijedor?

utterances.speaker: EDIN MRKALJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. K. SIMIC
utterances.text: Did he work in one of the departments, or was he attached to the central police station?

utterances.speaker: EDIN MRKALJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I can remember, he worked in the Ljubija police station department.

utterances.speaker: MR. K. SIMIC
utterances.text: Very well. Do you have any information saying that Mr. Aliskovic participated in an incident in the second half of May in the Prijedor municipality?

utterances.speaker: EDIN MRKALJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. K. SIMIC
utterances.text: What was it?

utterances.speaker: EDIN MRKALJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was an incident at a checkpoint in the village of Hambarine. As the house of Aziz Aliskovic was about 100 metres from the checkpoint, his name was linked to that incident. Then an ultimatum was addressed to him demanding that he surrender.

utterances.speaker: MR. K. SIMIC
utterances.text: Who organised that checkpoint close to Mr. Aliskovic's house, where the incident occurred? Was it a checkpoint of the legal authorities?

utterances.speaker: EDIN MRKALJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. K. SIMIC
utterances.text: Who organised it?

utterances.speaker: EDIN MRKALJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: The public security station of Prijedor.

utterances.speaker: MR. K. SIMIC
utterances.text: Were you on duty in that period at that checkpoint?

utterances.speaker: EDIN MRKALJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. K. SIMIC
utterances.text: Were there any casualties in that incident, and deaths?

utterances.speaker: EDIN MRKALJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I can remember, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. K. SIMIC
utterances.text: Do you know whether the Prijedor Public Security Station instituted disciplinary, and later criminal proceedings against Mr. Aliskovic, who was suspected of having participated in the incident when two or three persons were killed?

utterances.speaker: EDIN MRKALJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. The procedure was instituted by the Serb Democratic Party and its headquarters, by its propaganda over the radio.

utterances.speaker: MR. K. SIMIC
utterances.text: I'm talking about the Prijedor Public Security Station, the legal one, not the Serb Democratic Party. Three men were killed. Doesn't this imply the obligation of the public security station, not the Serbs, to institute an investigation, and if Mr. Aliskovic is found to be guilty, to punish him?

utterances.speaker: EDIN MRKALJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: The Serb side took over power, so the public security station stopped functioning, and thereby there was no possibility of establishing the actual state of affairs, the facts of the case.

utterances.speaker: MR. K. SIMIC
utterances.text: But a moment ago you told me that the checkpoint was established by the Prijedor Public Security Station, and that is why I'm asking you.

utterances.speaker: EDIN MRKALJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: The checkpoint had been established much earlier, before the Serb takeover.

utterances.speaker: MR. K. SIMIC
utterances.text: Well, talking about that, when did the Serb side take over power in Prijedor?

utterances.speaker: EDIN MRKALJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I can recollect, at the beginning of May.

utterances.speaker: MR. K. SIMIC
utterances.text: Regardless of the fact that you were on sick-leave, you moved about, and so on. Were you present at a large rally of members of the police or members of the Prijedor Public Security Station, chaired by Mr. Hasan Talundzic, on the 29th of April, 1992? Let me help you. The meeting was motivated by the security situation and the situation in the public security station itself. That was the reason for the meeting.

utterances.speaker: EDIN MRKALJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. K. SIMIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Still in this area of questioning, could you tell the Trial Chamber whether, at the end of May, there was an armed conflict in the town of Prijedor itself?

utterances.speaker: MS. HOLLIS
utterances.text: Excuse me, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Madam Hollis.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOLLIS
utterances.text: Your Honour, perhaps that question could be rephrased. The existence of an armed conflict is a legal determination. Perhaps it could be phrased in more factual terms as to what occurred.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Simic.

utterances.speaker: MR. K. SIMIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, in the course of the month of May that year, a most unfortunate one, I can call it, for the whole region, many things occurred -- there was a conflict in Hambarine; there was another one -- and that is why I wanted the witness to tell us. I accept the suggestion.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Excuse me, Mr. Simic, you said that many facts occurred. Well, put your question in those terms, what took place. Don't ask for conclusions. You need several steps to get to that point.

utterances.speaker: MR. K. SIMIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. K. SIMIC
utterances.text: What happened at the end of May?

utterances.speaker: EDIN MRKALJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Could you repeat the question?

utterances.speaker: MR. K. SIMIC
utterances.text: Did anything happen at the end of May in the town of Prijedor itself?

utterances.speaker: EDIN MRKALJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I can remember, there was an incident when the Serb army killed four civilians from the village of Brezicani, Prijedor municipality. That incident occurred -- I remember that -- an armed incident against unarmed civilians who were coming back from the fields on a tractor.

utterances.speaker: MR. K. SIMIC
utterances.text: Mr. Mrkalj, my question related to the town itself. That is why I phrased my question as I did. And I apologise to Ms. Hollis.

utterances.speaker: EDIN MRKALJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: The area where the crime occurred belongs to the municipality of Prijedor.

utterances.speaker: MR. K. SIMIC
utterances.text: In the course of the night, were there any military actions of larger proportions?

utterances.speaker: EDIN MRKALJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I can recollect, it was in response, by to me unknown persons, that a conflict occurred in Prijedor. But what actually happened, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. K. SIMIC
utterances.text: Mr. Mrkalj, did you participate in that conflict?

utterances.speaker: EDIN MRKALJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: What conflict?

utterances.speaker: MR. K. SIMIC
utterances.text: The one you just described.

utterances.speaker: EDIN MRKALJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: I said I heard about it.

utterances.speaker: MR. K. SIMIC
utterances.text: Very well. Thank you. When did you hand in your weapons to the public security station in Prijedor?

utterances.speaker: EDIN MRKALJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: When that was demanded of me.

utterances.speaker: MR. K. SIMIC
utterances.text: On what date?

utterances.speaker: EDIN MRKALJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I can recollect, I think it must have been the 1st of June.

utterances.speaker: MR. K. SIMIC
utterances.text: Who asked you to hand in your weapons, and in what way?

utterances.speaker: EDIN MRKALJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: The night before, a reserve policeman came and conveyed to me the message that the authorities requested that I appear at the public security station in Prijedor with my personal weapons. When I asked him what would happen if I do not appear, he answered, "You know what happened in Hambarine, when Aliskovic did not surrender." I had very little time to think things over.

utterances.speaker: MR. K. SIMIC
utterances.text: And knowing the situation, did you take the weapons or not?

utterances.speaker: EDIN MRKALJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. K. SIMIC
utterances.text: What happened that day when you brought your weapons, to the public security station, of course?

utterances.speaker: EDIN MRKALJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: When we reached the station, I was searched, my personal belongings were seized from me, and I was taken to the first floor, to the crime department, for processing.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Simic, we are being told that it is not possible to distinguish between the questions and answers, so could you please make a break between your questions and the answers. Because you're speaking the same languages, and the interpreters are having difficulty in following the questions and the answers.

utterances.speaker: MR. K. SIMIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. K. SIMIC
utterances.text: On that occasion did you make the normal, regular, standard statement?

utterances.speaker: EDIN MRKALJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: What do you mean?

utterances.speaker: MR. K. SIMIC
utterances.text: On that occasion did you make a statement in the police station of Prijedor to one of the investigators, or inspectors, as we used to call them?

utterances.speaker: EDIN MRKALJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: There was an interrogation. And when I say "interrogation," that also implies what you're asking.

utterances.speaker: MR. K. SIMIC
utterances.text: Who questioned you?

utterances.speaker: EDIN MRKALJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Members of the crime service of the public security station.

utterances.speaker: MR. K. SIMIC
utterances.text: Do you know their names?

utterances.speaker: EDIN MRKALJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. K. SIMIC
utterances.text: What were their names?

utterances.speaker: EDIN MRKALJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: There were several of them. Mira Jankovic, Nenad Lakic, Gostimir Modic, and there was another person whom I didn't know. I think that he had fled from Croatia, where he used to work in the Ministry of the Interior, SUP.

utterances.speaker: MR. K. SIMIC
utterances.text: On that occasion was any kind of report drawn up? Did you sign anything?

utterances.speaker: EDIN MRKALJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: They questioned me for about three hours, they took notes, but I was not given anything to sign.

utterances.speaker: MR. K. SIMIC
utterances.text: What did you tell them?

utterances.speaker: EDIN MRKALJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: I told them the -- I answered the questions they put to me.

utterances.speaker: MR. K. SIMIC
utterances.text: But can you tell us the gist of those questions and answers?

utterances.speaker: EDIN MRKALJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Could you make that clearer?

utterances.speaker: MR. K. SIMIC
utterances.text: What were they in interested in?

utterances.speaker: EDIN MRKALJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: They were interested in the situation in the area I came from.

utterances.speaker: MR. K. SIMIC
utterances.text: Linked to the harvest or actions or arming?

utterances.speaker: EDIN MRKALJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: There were a great many questions; many, many.

utterances.speaker: MR. K. SIMIC
utterances.text: Thank you. You were transferred to Omarska. When and how?

utterances.speaker: EDIN MRKALJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was first imprisoned.

utterances.speaker: MR. K. SIMIC
utterances.text: You spent a night there. After that night you were transferred to Omarska.

utterances.speaker: EDIN MRKALJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Could you please give me a question rather than a statement? It would be easier for me to give you answers.

utterances.speaker: MR. K. SIMIC
utterances.text: When did you go to Omarska?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm sorry. Mr. Simic, I apologise, but I think that the witness has answered that question during the examination-in-chief. Perhaps you could put your questions directly, and in that way you would get a direct answer maybe. Because the witness has already explained what happened to him. So please put a direct question to the witness, if possible, Mr. Simic.

utterances.speaker: MR. K. SIMIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, it is true that according to the transcript and my own notes, he did talk about this, but there are reasons why I wish to refer back to these events, and that is why I would like the witness to answer questions which we consider to be very important for us, and in view of the examination-in-chief of Ms. Hollis.

utterances.speaker: MR. K. SIMIC
utterances.text: By what means were you transported to Omarska?

utterances.speaker: EDIN MRKALJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: By bus.

utterances.speaker: MR. K. SIMIC
utterances.text: Was it a bus carrying other prisoners, or something else?

utterances.speaker: EDIN MRKALJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Members of the crime service.

utterances.speaker: MR. K. SIMIC
utterances.text: So let's speed things up. You reached Omarska. Could you, at least roughly, tell us how you moved about from your arrival in Omarska until you left? In which building were you placed and in what time periods?

utterances.speaker: EDIN MRKALJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is very hard for me to tell you with any precision.

utterances.speaker: MR. K. SIMIC
utterances.text: But I said roughly.

utterances.speaker: EDIN MRKALJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: What does "roughly" mean?

utterances.speaker: MR. K. SIMIC
utterances.text: Approximately where were you held upon your arrival in Omarska and how much time did you spend there, to make it simpler.

utterances.speaker: EDIN MRKALJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was -- for the first few days, I think until the 6th, if I remember well, I was in this building here. Can I point? This building [indicates].

utterances.speaker: MR. K. SIMIC
utterances.text: Is that the hangar?

utterances.speaker: EDIN MRKALJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, the hangar.

utterances.speaker: MR. K. SIMIC
utterances.text: So for the first few days, until the 6th, you were in the hangar?

utterances.speaker: EDIN MRKALJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, as far as I can recollect.

utterances.speaker: MR. K. SIMIC
utterances.text: After the hangar, where were you?

utterances.speaker: EDIN MRKALJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: At the pista.

utterances.speaker: MR. K. SIMIC
utterances.text: How much time did you spend there?

utterances.speaker: EDIN MRKALJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I can remember, about 40 days, something like that.

utterances.speaker: MR. K. SIMIC
utterances.text: During your testimony you spoke about the transportation of other prisoners. You arrived in Omarska on the 6th. Did you personally, after the 6th, see, in view of where you were held, the arrival of buses or other means of transportation bringing in prisoners?

utterances.speaker: EDIN MRKALJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, when I was at the pista. I was at the pista. I could see.

utterances.speaker: MR. K. SIMIC
utterances.text: So after the 6th you are saying that buses with prisoners came to Omarska?

utterances.speaker: EDIN MRKALJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't say buses. Could you please put your question in concrete terms? I don't know what you want me to say.

utterances.speaker: MR. K. SIMIC
utterances.text: I want you to tell us the truth.

utterances.speaker: EDIN MRKALJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: I am telling the truth.

utterances.speaker: MR. K. SIMIC
utterances.text: So let me rephrase and simplify the question. Did you personally see the bringing in of new prisoners after your detention and after you left the hangar?

utterances.speaker: EDIN MRKALJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, from the pista I could see perfectly well.

utterances.speaker: MR. K. SIMIC
utterances.text: I didn't say whether you could see it; I said whether you did see it.

utterances.speaker: EDIN MRKALJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did see.

utterances.speaker: MR. K. SIMIC
utterances.text: What did you see?

utterances.speaker: EDIN MRKALJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Persons being brought in.

utterances.speaker: MR. K. SIMIC
utterances.text: In what way?

utterances.speaker: EDIN MRKALJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: They were brought in in an official vehicle, the so-called Marica, black Marica.

utterances.speaker: MR. K. SIMIC
utterances.text: During your testimony you reached the point when you were questioned, when you were interrogated, but you didn't tell us at all whether you were interrogated or not.

utterances.speaker: EDIN MRKALJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I was. I was interrogated many, many times.

utterances.speaker: MR. K. SIMIC
utterances.text: When were you interrogated for the first time?

utterances.speaker: EDIN MRKALJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: When I was first brought in, the first day.

utterances.speaker: MR. K. SIMIC
utterances.text: Were you taken from the vehicle immediately to the first floor of the administration building?

utterances.speaker: EDIN MRKALJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. K. SIMIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I should like to ask the usher to show Exhibit 3/77P, a sketch of the administration building, so that we can be a little bit more precise, as this is something we have not touched upon at all.

utterances.speaker: MR. K. SIMIC
utterances.text: Mr. Mrkalj, you have a sketch in front of you of the administration building, the first floor of that building, where those interrogations took place. In which room were you interrogated the first time? You put it at the 2nd of June, 1992.

utterances.speaker: EDIN MRKALJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know for sure but I know it was on the right-hand side. But which one, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. K. SIMIC
utterances.text: When you were interrogated for the second time?

utterances.speaker: EDIN MRKALJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was another room and another group of investigators.

utterances.speaker: MR. K. SIMIC
utterances.text: Sorry. When you were interrogated for the first time, who were the interrogators?

utterances.speaker: EDIN MRKALJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: There were two inspectors, as they said, whom I didn't know, and they introduced themselves as people who used to have the same job in the Republic of Croatia, in the area of Pakrac. I could not identify them; they didn't give me their names. The first question they asked, they said, "Your answer to our first question will decide your fate, whether you will survive or not."

utterances.speaker: MR. K. SIMIC
utterances.text: Did they have any notes about the interrogations with you in the public security station in Prijedor of the 1st of June?

utterances.speaker: EDIN MRKALJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: They had a lot of papers on the basis of which they questioned me.

utterances.speaker: MR. K. SIMIC
utterances.text: When were you interrogated for the second time?

utterances.speaker: EDIN MRKALJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Very shortly after that, almost daily, until the actual trial, when the Serb court, they organised a kind of trial at the end of all those interrogations; a Serb court, that's what they said, of the Serb Republic. I remember they gave me a defence counsel; unfortunately, he was worse than the prosecution.

utterances.speaker: MR. K. SIMIC
utterances.text: Where was this trial organised?

utterances.speaker: EDIN MRKALJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was organised in the administration building.

utterances.speaker: MR. K. SIMIC
utterances.text: On the first floor?

utterances.speaker: EDIN MRKALJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, on the first floor.

utterances.speaker: MR. K. SIMIC
utterances.text: Could you tell us in what room? You have the sketch in front of you.

utterances.speaker: EDIN MRKALJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was taken to the first floor. By then already I had to look down, and this was very strict. You couldn't look left or right; you had to look at your own feet. Then I think we were taken to the large room to the right, but anyway, I had to look down all the time. I was placed in a chair --

utterances.speaker: MR. K. SIMIC
utterances.text: Mr. Mrkalj, during those frequent interrogations, did anyone you knew among the inspectors, people who used to work in the Prijedor Public Security Station, interrogate you?

utterances.speaker: EDIN MRKALJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: On the umpteenth occasion --

utterances.speaker: MR. K. SIMIC
utterances.text: If you don't know, you don't have to tell us.

utterances.speaker: EDIN MRKALJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: I remember there was this Nenad Lakic, a former colleague of mine and then --

utterances.speaker: MR. K. SIMIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Can I ask you what penalty or punishment they brought against you?

utterances.speaker: EDIN MRKALJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was told at the end of the trial, because there was a typist who was typing down everything, and I was told at the end -- I was asked, do I want to sign, do I want to sign. I had no choice. I said I would sign.

utterances.speaker: MR. K. SIMIC
utterances.text: What?

utterances.speaker: EDIN MRKALJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: What she was typing and the questions that they were asking me about, general questions about everything. But the verdict, I wasn't told. They called a guide, who would take people back, to take me away, and I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. K. SIMIC
utterances.text: Do you know who your defence attorney was?

utterances.speaker: EDIN MRKALJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do. His name was Triso, Triso from Prijedor.

utterances.speaker: MR. K. SIMIC
utterances.text: Mr. Mrkalj, I understand and know about the time when you were detained and the time that has elapsed. But can you tell us with any certainty, indicate any one of the rooms that you went into? If you can't, you can't.

utterances.speaker: EDIN MRKALJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: I told you, I was questioned on a number of occasions and in several different rooms. But the system was to disorientate one, so for a time I was sure it was the first or the second room on the right, and then those on the left were a bit larger, and so on --

utterances.speaker: MR. K. SIMIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Mrkalj. Let us now go on to the one but last area.

utterances.speaker: MR. K. SIMIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I should like to ask the usher to have the witness shown document D17/1 and to have D17/1A be given to the Prosecution and the Trial Chamber so that they can follow.

utterances.speaker: MR. K. SIMIC
utterances.text: You have the text in front of you.

utterances.speaker: EDIN MRKALJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's not very legible; I can't read properly.

utterances.speaker: MR. K. SIMIC
utterances.text: We'll read it together. Mr. Mrkalj, during your testimony, when you came to the identification process, you recognised Mr. Simo Drljaca; you spoke about him. Now, tell us, who was Simo Drljaca?

utterances.speaker: EDIN MRKALJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: He was the man who came to replace the chief of the Prijedor Public Security Station.

utterances.speaker: MR. K. SIMIC
utterances.text: In the territory of Prijedor municipality, did a Crisis Staff of the Prijedor municipality function at all?

utterances.speaker: EDIN MRKALJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: When do you mean?

utterances.speaker: MR. K. SIMIC
utterances.text: We are talking about May, when Mr. Drljaca became chief of the security station.

utterances.speaker: EDIN MRKALJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: You mean the Serbian Crisis Staff?

utterances.speaker: MR. K. SIMIC
utterances.text: Very well. The Serbian Crisis Staff of Prijedor municipality. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: EDIN MRKALJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. K. SIMIC
utterances.text: Mr. Drljaca, as the chief of the public security station, was he a member of that Crisis Staff?

utterances.speaker: EDIN MRKALJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I recall, yes, he was.

utterances.speaker: MR. K. SIMIC
utterances.text: What competencies or authority did the Serbian Crisis Staff of Prijedor municipality have?

utterances.speaker: EDIN MRKALJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't really tell you that. I don't know what they had in their documents and acts.

utterances.speaker: MR. K. SIMIC
utterances.text: And in practice?

utterances.speaker: EDIN MRKALJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: How do you mean "in practice"?

utterances.speaker: MR. K. SIMIC
utterances.text: Did they make any statements, anything of that kind? Did you happen to hear that via the media?

utterances.speaker: EDIN MRKALJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, on the radio.

utterances.speaker: MR. K. SIMIC
utterances.text: Did you know Mr. Drljaca?

utterances.speaker: EDIN MRKALJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: I met him, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. K. SIMIC
utterances.text: You have before you a document and we'll read through it together, the sections that we want to comment. We'll skip over the heading and we'll go on to "Centre of Security Services of Banja Luka, the Public Security Station of Prijedor, Strictly Confidential, number 11-12-20." The date is the 31st of May, 1992, that is, two days before you were brought to Omarska. In the introduction it states as follows: "With a view to the speedy and effective establishment of peace on the territory of Prijedor municipality, and in accordance with the decision of the Crisis Staff, I hereby order the following," and after that it goes on to state -- that is to say, let us turn over the page, and on page 3 it says: "Chief of the Public Security Station, Simo Drljaca." Page 3. There is a stamp as well.

utterances.speaker: EDIN MRKALJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Who is doing the questioning now, you or the man sitting next to you?

utterances.speaker: MR. K. SIMIC
utterances.text: I am putting the questions to you and I am assisted by my colleague.

utterances.speaker: EDIN MRKALJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Could you repeat the question, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. K. SIMIC
utterances.text: On page 3, is there a stamp and does it say "Chief of the Public Security Service, Simo Drljaca"?

utterances.speaker: EDIN MRKALJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's what it says, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. K. SIMIC
utterances.text: Is this an order, as you said yesterday, by the number one man in the public security station of Prijedor?

utterances.speaker: EDIN MRKALJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: For me, this is nothing.

utterances.speaker: MR. K. SIMIC
utterances.text: I am speaking about the document from the aspects of the way I have read it out. Is it an order or --

utterances.speaker: EDIN MRKALJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot comment on the aspects.

utterances.speaker: MR. K. SIMIC
utterances.text: We are talking about the order itself, the document itself. We'll come to the various points in that order.

utterances.speaker: EDIN MRKALJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I can't comment.

utterances.speaker: MR. K. SIMIC
utterances.text: Would you yourself please read out point 6 of this order.

utterances.speaker: EDIN MRKALJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: You want me to read it out?

utterances.speaker: MR. K. SIMIC
utterances.text: Yes, please, you read it out. You have it in front of you. You don't have to read it aloud; you can read it to yourself.

utterances.speaker: EDIN MRKALJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have read it.

utterances.speaker: MR. K. SIMIC
utterances.text: Is that an order by the chief of the public security station to the department of the Omarska police station to provide security -- let us use the term "camp" -- to provide security for the camp?

utterances.speaker: EDIN MRKALJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's what it says.

utterances.speaker: MR. K. SIMIC
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Let us now read point 3 because it concerns individuals that you knew, or I'll read it and you can follow it for purposes of the transcript. [As read] "The further work and selection of detained individuals will be continued by a mixed committee of inspectors of national, public, and military security who must be organised according to this same mixed principle. For their work, the responsible individuals are Mirko Jesic, Ranko Mijic, and Lieutenant Colonel Majstorovic." Mr. Mrkalj, is that an order to three services -- the main security service, public security service, and military security service -- to perform certain investigations, and that this order appoints individuals on behalf of all of these -- that is to say, from all of these departments?

utterances.speaker: EDIN MRKALJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is what it says.

utterances.speaker: MR. K. SIMIC
utterances.text: Do you know Ranko Mijic?

utterances.speaker: EDIN MRKALJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. K. SIMIC
utterances.text: What was he? What was his function in the public security service?

utterances.speaker: EDIN MRKALJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: He was chief of the crime department.

utterances.speaker: MR. K. SIMIC
utterances.text: Do you know Mr. Jesic?

utterances.speaker: EDIN MRKALJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. K. SIMIC
utterances.text: What was he?

utterances.speaker: EDIN MRKALJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: He worked in matters of state security, as far as I recall.

utterances.speaker: MR. K. SIMIC
utterances.text: Do you know Lieutenant Colonel Majstorovic?

utterances.speaker: EDIN MRKALJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not quite sure.

utterances.speaker: MR. K. SIMIC
utterances.text: I should now like to ask you to look at point 7, paragraph 7 of the order, which is on page 2. And I read as follows: "The mine's Management shall organise --"

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Simic, you needn't repeat the document. We have the document in front of us. You can just ask the question. We have the document, the witness has the document, so why read the document?

utterances.speaker: MR. K. SIMIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, I thought that by this we would save time because I would have --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. Give the witness a little time to read the paragraph himself and then go on to asking your question.

utterances.speaker: MR. K. SIMIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. K. SIMIC
utterances.text: Would you read sentence 1 of paragraph 7. Mr. Mrkalj, I see you've read it.

utterances.speaker: EDIN MRKALJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, you see, I haven't read it. You can't see well. I see that you don't see very well because I haven't read it. The word "u koju" is written separately, two words. But, yes, I have completed reading now.

utterances.speaker: MR. K. SIMIC
utterances.text: Is this an order to the mine's management of Ljubija to organise meals in conformity with the members of the military quartermaster service?

utterances.speaker: EDIN MRKALJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's only what it says on paper.

utterances.speaker: MR. K. SIMIC
utterances.text: Please go on to read the second sentence of paragraph 7 so that we can wind this up.

utterances.speaker: EDIN MRKALJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is a catastrophe.

utterances.speaker: MR. K. SIMIC
utterances.text: I expect an answer, Witness, not a comment. Is it an order that the Mines' Management should organise a regular cleaning of the compound and everything else?

utterances.speaker: EDIN MRKALJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is what it states.

utterances.speaker: MR. K. SIMIC
utterances.text: I should now like to ask you to read paragraph 11 on that same page.

utterances.speaker: EDIN MRKALJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: It says here --

utterances.speaker: MR. K. SIMIC
utterances.text: Very well. You've read it, then.

utterances.speaker: EDIN MRKALJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: I haven't read it, because I can't see the number. I can't see what time it says.

utterances.speaker: MR. K. SIMIC
utterances.text: It says 1200 hours.

utterances.speaker: EDIN MRKALJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: In my text it says "unit," and then there's nothing else, so I can't find my way.

utterances.speaker: MR. K. SIMIC
utterances.text: Is this an order that the Security Services coordinators are duty-bound every day, at a particular hour, to send in a report to the chief of the Prijedor Public Security Station?

utterances.speaker: EDIN MRKALJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is what it says here.

utterances.speaker: MR. K. SIMIC
utterances.text: Who are the coordinators? And if you haven't remembered, we can go back to paragraph 3 on page 1 to remind you.

utterances.speaker: EDIN MRKALJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: What do you want me to answer now?

utterances.speaker: MR. K. SIMIC
utterances.text: Are the coordinators Mr. Jesic, Mr. Mijic, and Lieutenant Colonel Majstorovic? Were they them, the coordinators?

utterances.speaker: EDIN MRKALJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, we already said that.

utterances.speaker: MR. K. SIMIC
utterances.text: Very well. Thank you. To whom is this report sent? Give us his name. The chief of the Prijedor Public Security Station, what was the chief's name?

utterances.speaker: EDIN MRKALJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Simo Drljaca.

utterances.speaker: MR. K. SIMIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Now read, if you will, paragraph 12 of that same order. Mr. Mrkalj, according to this order, is it also the duty of the chief of security to proceed in the same manner with respect to the functioning of the Security Service?

utterances.speaker: EDIN MRKALJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Would you let me read through it, please? You seem to be in a hurry.

utterances.speaker: MR. K. SIMIC
utterances.text: No, I'm in no hurry at all. Take your time. Read it through at your leisure.

utterances.speaker: EDIN MRKALJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: I've read the paragraph.

utterances.speaker: MR. K. SIMIC
utterances.text: Let me repeat: Is that also an order to the chief of security that he is duty-bound to proceed in the same way with security matters?

utterances.speaker: EDIN MRKALJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's what it says.

utterances.speaker: MR. K. SIMIC
utterances.text: Very well. That's what it says, then. And to wind up now, I should like to ask you to read through paragraph 17 of the same order very carefully.

utterances.speaker: EDIN MRKALJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: I've read it.

utterances.speaker: MR. K. SIMIC
utterances.text: Is this an order that the control and supervision of the execution of this order shall be performed by the police chief, Dusan Jankovic?

utterances.speaker: EDIN MRKALJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can only note that that is what it says here.

utterances.speaker: MR. K. SIMIC
utterances.text: Now, on page -- on the same page, Mr. Mrkalj, staying with that page. In the police, in our legal system, when a legal act is sent out to anybody, an order, decision, or any similar document, does it state to whom -- the addressee, as to whom these documents are sent? Is that also stipulated?

utterances.speaker: EDIN MRKALJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. K. SIMIC
utterances.text: Thank you. I heard you say yes. And in that sense, I should like to ask you to read what it says after paragraph 17. It says: Sent to -- copies sent to --

utterances.speaker: EDIN MRKALJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: It says here "1. Crisis Staff," et cetera.

utterances.speaker: MR. K. SIMIC
utterances.text: Very well. The Crisis Staff. So copies are sent there; right?

utterances.speaker: EDIN MRKALJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, you told me to read through it.

utterances.speaker: MR. K. SIMIC
utterances.text: Very well. Yes, please continue.

utterances.speaker: EDIN MRKALJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Now there are the coordinators.

utterances.speaker: MR. K. SIMIC
utterances.text: It says "security services coordinators."

utterances.speaker: EDIN MRKALJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't see what it says next.

utterances.speaker: MR. K. SIMIC
utterances.text: In my document it is the CBS Banja Luka. Then we have the police chief. Who is the police chief, in conformity with paragraph 17? Dusan Jankovic; is that it?

utterances.speaker: EDIN MRKALJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, it says what it says. Somebody wrote that, so that's what it says.

utterances.speaker: MR. K. SIMIC
utterances.text: Jankovic, Dusan. Next it says "security chief." Does it say that?

utterances.speaker: EDIN MRKALJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's what it says.

utterances.speaker: MR. K. SIMIC
utterances.text: Does it say "General Manager, RJR, the Ljubija Iron Ore Mines"?

utterances.speaker: EDIN MRKALJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. K. SIMIC
utterances.text: Does it say "files" or "archives"?

utterances.speaker: EDIN MRKALJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: It does.

utterances.speaker: MR. K. SIMIC
utterances.text: Mr. Mrkalj, is this document, this act, with clear-cut instructions, was it sent to those individuals who are duty-bound to act upon it?

utterances.speaker: EDIN MRKALJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's what it says. Now, I don't know what --

utterances.speaker: MR. K. SIMIC
utterances.text: Very well. Thank you. It says that copies were sent to the commander. Does it say the commander of the camp?

utterances.speaker: EDIN MRKALJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, it does not.

utterances.speaker: MR. K. SIMIC
utterances.text: May I hold your attention for one moment longer on paragraph 11 of this same document.

utterances.speaker: EDIN MRKALJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. K. SIMIC
utterances.text: To whom did all these individuals have to submit reports?

utterances.speaker: EDIN MRKALJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: To the chief. To the chief of the public security station.

utterances.speaker: MR. K. SIMIC
utterances.text: Thank you. When we spoke about reports and who tables reports, is the term "commander," "lead deputy," does it say they submit reports to the chief of the public security station in any way?

utterances.speaker: EDIN MRKALJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: In these papers, you mean?

utterances.speaker: MR. K. SIMIC
utterances.text: Yes, in these documents, in the document we're looking at.

utterances.speaker: EDIN MRKALJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, it does not.

utterances.speaker: MR. K. SIMIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Mrkalj. Yesterday -- rather, the day before, in your testimony you mentioned that you have certain repercussions with respect to your health and that you have had dealings with psychiatrists, psychologists. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: EDIN MRKALJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. K. SIMIC
utterances.text: Could you tell us what kind of -- what the manifestations of your illness or the consequences of what you have suffered are?

utterances.speaker: EDIN MRKALJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: My psychological state is very difficult, and it was brought on as a consequence of what happened in the camp.

utterances.speaker: MR. K. SIMIC
utterances.text: Yes, but could you tell us how this is manifested? Will you wait for me to finish? The Judges have been drawing my attention to ask concrete questions, so I'm asking you about the manifestations.

utterances.speaker: EDIN MRKALJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Nobody has yet warned me.

utterances.speaker: MR. K. SIMIC
utterances.text: Well, we were warned earlier on and you were asked to answer my questions.

utterances.speaker: EDIN MRKALJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: So you were cautioned, not me.

utterances.speaker: MR. K. SIMIC
utterances.text: I think both of us were cautioned.

utterances.speaker: EDIN MRKALJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I have every respect for the work you do, and the consequences of the camp and what happened in the camp are as follows: The day before yesterday you witnessed a very -- quite an unusual event which took place here, and I see that everybody was present during the identification of accused, of a witness. When I turned around and had to point out the real name, I had a terrible scene conjured up in my mind, come to mind.

utterances.speaker: MR. K. SIMIC
utterances.text: I'm not asking you that. We completed that question. I'm just asking you the manifestations of your health condition.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOLLIS
utterances.text: Your Honour, I object to this intervention. I believe that the witness was answering exactly what was asked, the consequences, and he was explaining what occurred in his mind when he looked. So I believe indeed he was answering a question. I would ask the Defence counsel to allow him to complete the answer.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: We were not getting the interpretation. I do apologise.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can the Defence counsel hear now? Yes? Mr. Simic, a response to Ms. Hollis' objection.

utterances.speaker: MR. K. SIMIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, I asked the witness to say what he has been treated for, the symptoms that he has been treated for, and not to go back to a scene that has already passed. And Ms. Hollis can go back to it, of course, during her re-examination, but I here and now am interested in the diagnosis, in what Mr. -- I beg your pardon -- what Mr. Mrkalj's diagnosis is.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Simic, the same question was raised by Ms. Hollis the day before yesterday, the consequences. The same question was raised the day before yesterday by Ms. Hollis, what the consequences are. Now, what is your precise question?

utterances.speaker: MR. K. SIMIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, I withdraw my question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, if you want to ask the witness what the consequences are, you are asking exactly the same question that Ms. Hollis asked.

utterances.speaker: MR. K. SIMIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I withdraw the question in view of the fact that Ms. Hollis has already posed it, and I have completed my cross-examination. Thank you, Mr. Mrkalj, for your assistance.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Thank you, Mr. Simic. Mr. Fila, I think that this would be an opportune moment to take a break. We rise for half an hour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Please be seated. Mr. Jovan Simic, is there a problem?

utterances.speaker: MR. J. SIMIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, concerning the problem we raised prior to the break, we have spoken to the Registrar. Mr. Rhodes said that such an order was issued upon the request of the Prosecution. I have spoken to my learned friend, Ms. Hollis, who told me that such a request had not come from the Prosecution. I've spoken to the Registry again and I was advised to very briefly see with the Prosecution whether they object and whether they oppose my client being transported together with the other accused so that this problem can be resolved and the accused may be allowed to leave. In that way, the Registrar would be informed that the Prosecution has nothing against such a decision.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Ms. Hollis, have you any comment to make?

utterances.speaker: MS. HOLLIS
utterances.text: First of all, Your Honour, the Prosecution is very surprised to learn that it's upon our request that such a thing would happen. But as regards this particular request that Defence counsel for Mr. Prcac has made, of course we have no objection to anything that is required by the health of this accused, and we would have no objection to a return to the detention facility very quickly after the close of proceedings each day if that is what is required for the accused's health.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much, Ms. Hollis. Madam Registrar, you will take note of this so that the Registrar may decide, as it is not a matter for the Chamber. But the Chamber does recommend that this matter be taken into consideration. We're going to continue now with the cross-examination of this witness, and it is now Mr. Fila's turn to ask questions. Mr. Fila, please take care to make breaks between questions and answers; otherwise, the interpreters will find it hard to follow.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. I will pay attention.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: Good morning, Witness. I am Toma Fila, representing Radic. I hope you're feeling better. I was rather worried yesterday about your health. During your examination-in-chief, you said that on the 10th of April you left your employment in the public security station in Prijedor; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: EDIN MRKALJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I stopped working.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: Fine. During the examination-in-chief, you used the words "rules," "the book of rules," and so on. What I'm interested in is whether you know the exact title of those rules.

utterances.speaker: EDIN MRKALJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: I've already said once what the name of that book is.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: Is it "The Rules on the Work of Employees of the Internal Affairs Service"?

utterances.speaker: EDIN MRKALJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: So that is the right name. Was it a book which you studied during your training? And those rules were still in force when you stopped working, is the expression that you prefer.

utterances.speaker: EDIN MRKALJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: After leaving the public security station, do you have any idea how the work was done?

utterances.speaker: EDIN MRKALJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: What do you mean?

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: I mean after the takeover of power, the new organisation, Simo Drljaca, and all the rest, do you know which legal regulations governed their work?

utterances.speaker: EDIN MRKALJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: You mentioned the name of Zeljko Meakic.

utterances.speaker: EDIN MRKALJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: Later you said that you left the Omarska camp in August, when the camp was disbanded.

utterances.speaker: EDIN MRKALJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: Was Zeljko Meakic present at the time, when that happened? I'm talking about the call-out.

utterances.speaker: EDIN MRKALJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think he was.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: What was his position in the camp throughout that time, if you know?

utterances.speaker: EDIN MRKALJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: According to correct information that reached me, his function ceased some two weeks prior to the disbanding of the camp, the post of camp commander.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: During those two weeks, those last two weeks, did the situation in the camp improve at all? Let me help you. There were some journalists and so on, to remind you of that period.

utterances.speaker: EDIN MRKALJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: Do you remember that some people came to pay a visit?

utterances.speaker: EDIN MRKALJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: There was a visit, yes, but nothing improved. Just when they came, there was some cosmetic improvements.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: You mentioned some sort of a trial -- drink your water in peace.

utterances.speaker: EDIN MRKALJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: -- and a lawyer Triso. Was he a lawyer?

utterances.speaker: EDIN MRKALJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, a lawyer.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: From Prijedor?

utterances.speaker: EDIN MRKALJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: You also mentioned a typist.

utterances.speaker: EDIN MRKALJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: Do you know her name, perhaps?

utterances.speaker: EDIN MRKALJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Slavica.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: Slavica. Was she perhaps from the public security station in Prijedor?

utterances.speaker: EDIN MRKALJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: So they were those who came there?

utterances.speaker: EDIN MRKALJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: You said that you knew Mladjo Radic from before and that his shift was the third shift, judging by a number worn on the backside of a T-shirt of one of the guards.

utterances.speaker: EDIN MRKALJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: How did you recognise the other shifts? Were they all wearing these numbers on their backs?

utterances.speaker: EDIN MRKALJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, they were not.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: But this one was called the third?

utterances.speaker: EDIN MRKALJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, by this number 3.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: Who do you know from that shift?

utterances.speaker: EDIN MRKALJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: From shift number 3?

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: Yes, in addition to Mladjo Radic.

utterances.speaker: EDIN MRKALJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mladjo Radic. I know him.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: Do you know anyone else?

utterances.speaker: EDIN MRKALJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I didn't know those people from before.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: And now? I mean, now have you remembered any one of them?

utterances.speaker: EDIN MRKALJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I didn't know them personally. They were people from the area.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: Can I say that neither then or now did you know the names of the persons in the third shift except for Mladjo Radic?

utterances.speaker: EDIN MRKALJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: I knew Mladjo Radic in person.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: So apart from him, you didn't know anyone else?

utterances.speaker: EDIN MRKALJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: When Dusko Tadic was beating you, that you told us about yesterday, was any guard present whose name you know?

utterances.speaker: EDIN MRKALJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Among those who were working there, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: You mentioned the role of Krkan in connection with some call-outs. I'm trying to remind you. And you said that you saw him. Were these call-outs of people who were going for interrogation to the administration building or some other kinds of call-outs?

utterances.speaker: EDIN MRKALJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: That depended on the situation. For instance, when that call-out was made, I couldn't see where the man went.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: You said they would come back beaten up.

utterances.speaker: EDIN MRKALJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: But where did they go to come back beaten up?

utterances.speaker: EDIN MRKALJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: It depended whether they would take the man out just to be beaten up or for interrogation, to be beaten up up there.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: Is that what you meant, that they were being taken for interrogation and beaten up there, when you said that you saw Mladjo Radic in the vicinity?

utterances.speaker: EDIN MRKALJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know what you're referring to.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: In the examination-in-chief, in answer to a question by Ms. Hollis, you said that once you saw Mladjo Radic being present when people were being called out for interrogation, and who were brought back beaten up. Is that what you meant?

utterances.speaker: EDIN MRKALJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: Was that the interrogation that was conducted in the administration building in a similar way as you were interrogated?

utterances.speaker: EDIN MRKALJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: People were beaten up every day.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: Are you referring to those interrogations?

utterances.speaker: EDIN MRKALJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: It depends on the situation you're referring to.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: You said you saw Krkan being present when people were being taken out for interrogation.

utterances.speaker: EDIN MRKALJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: Were they taken to the administration building?

utterances.speaker: EDIN MRKALJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: So where exactly did you see him? Was he standing or walking around?

utterances.speaker: EDIN MRKALJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: There, in front of the building, in front of the administration building. When the big beating occurred, he was --

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: Just tell us.

utterances.speaker: EDIN MRKALJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: What is marked with A21, the window up there. He was inside and I was standing where I could see him.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: Did you perhaps see whether he was carrying any weapons?

utterances.speaker: EDIN MRKALJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: You see, I didn't need to check whether he was armed or not. I didn't care. I didn't pay any attention to that.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: You said that a person from the security gave you certain information. That person, was he -- I'm sorry. Let me rephrase it. Was that the same person who informed you that Mladjo Radic was the shift leader? I'm not asking his name.

utterances.speaker: EDIN MRKALJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was told by that person, in addition to what I was able to see and hear.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: Was that one and the same person?

utterances.speaker: EDIN MRKALJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: Thank you. I'm not asking you his name. Did you know who wore that sports jersey with the number 3 on it?

utterances.speaker: EDIN MRKALJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't care. At the beginning of my treatment I was given instructions that it would be best not to polemicise and not to talk about what happened.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: Apart from you seeing Mladjo Radic up there, A21, as you said, in the administration building, is that what you were talking about in answer to Ms. Brenda Hollis' question?

utterances.speaker: EDIN MRKALJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: But that is where you said you saw him.

utterances.speaker: EDIN MRKALJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: I said in those various situations, at various times.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: In those various situations and times, I'm asking you for the place where you saw him.

utterances.speaker: EDIN MRKALJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: It depended on the event you are referring to.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: I'm asking you in what places you saw him.

utterances.speaker: EDIN MRKALJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: I've already told you: In various places, depending on what was happening.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. I have no further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much, Mr. Fila. Mr. Tosic, if you please.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOSIC
utterances.text: Good day to you, Mr. Mrkalj. I'm going to ask you a couple of questions. In Omarska, the incident of your beating by Dusko Tadic, you said that this occurred on the 16th of June, 1992, and you said that in that incident three other persons took part. Could you please tell us whether you know the names of those persons.

utterances.speaker: EDIN MRKALJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOSIC
utterances.text: In your testimony you also stated that you learnt subsequently the name of one of those three persons.

utterances.speaker: EDIN MRKALJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOSIC
utterances.text: Could you please tell us the name of that person.

utterances.speaker: EDIN MRKALJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOSIC
utterances.text: Will you tell us the first and last name of that person.

utterances.speaker: EDIN MRKALJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Zoran Vokic.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOSIC
utterances.text: Will you tell us: When that incident occurred, did you know the name of Zoran Vokic then, at the time?

utterances.speaker: EDIN MRKALJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOSIC
utterances.text: How much later during your stay in Omarska did you learn that it was Zoran Vokic?

utterances.speaker: EDIN MRKALJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was an assumption that it could have been that person.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOSIC
utterances.text: From whom did you learn the name of that person?

utterances.speaker: EDIN MRKALJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: From one of the detainees who thought that it might be that person.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOSIC
utterances.text: What were the comments exchanged between you and that detainee regarding the personality of Zoran Vokic? How did you come to that conclusion when talking to this detainee, the conclusion that it was Zoran Vokic?

utterances.speaker: EDIN MRKALJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Apparently he had seen him.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOSIC
utterances.text: While you were working in the Prijedor Police Station, did you know a person working in the police with a surname Vokic?

utterances.speaker: EDIN MRKALJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOSIC
utterances.text: Could you tell us the first name of that person?

utterances.speaker: EDIN MRKALJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Radovan Vokic.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOSIC
utterances.text: When you learnt of the name of Zoran Vokic, do you remember whether before Omarska you had any contact with that individual in your official dealings?

utterances.speaker: EDIN MRKALJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Something linked to traffic, but I wasn't sure. You can't remember all the people you deal with.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOSIC
utterances.text: Could you describe that person for us?

utterances.speaker: EDIN MRKALJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: The moments when I saw that person were such that I had very little chance to see him well, so I couldn't really describe him, in view of the condition I was in.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOSIC
utterances.text: Could you remember whether that person had something -- was wearing something unusual, something special, out of the ordinary, regarding the clothing he wore or his features or his appearance?

utterances.speaker: EDIN MRKALJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's rather hard for me to go back to those events, because for years I have been trying to forget them and to simply wipe them away from my memory. And I have answered these same questions so many times. I see no need for me to make the effort to look back.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOSIC
